local_articles.title: Isolated storms return to the Pittsburgh area on Sunday evening | First Alert Weather
local_articles.snippet: Today is a First Alert Weather Day, with decreasing clouds to start off our day and patchy fog, and highs in the low 80s with some sunshine for the Steelers game. There's a small chance for an isolated thunderstorm in the evening, which could be severe. Much of the day is dry, but there will be some isolated areas that get a quick downpour, or in the evening that could trigger flash flooding, especially with all of the rain from yesterday; it won't take much. We are under a marginal risk (1 out of 5) for severe weather, so confidence is lower that storms will become severe, but still stay weather aware for outdoor events mainly north of Pittsburgh this evening. After this weekend, Monday will be mostly sunny with highs in the low 70s, and comfortable! Tuesday will be back in the low 80s with sunshine and low humidity. questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-06 check (Exa + Sept 2 Reuters/Straits Times investigation 'US, China arm for space warfare: hunter satellites and orbital weapons'): No country has yet publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons. Crucially, the Sept 2 Reuters report sharpens the asymmetry in public-acknowledgment propensity: China's Foreign Ministry reiterated on the record that Beijing opposes space weaponization and insists its spaceplane/Shiyan missions are peaceful/experimental, and Moscow continues denying its nuclear ASAT program. By contrast, US SPACECOM head Gen. Stephen Whiting is openly arguing for an active warfighting posture and orbital interceptors, incoming Space Force CSO Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess led the newly disclosed US-UK orbital proximity operation, and the Space Force already broke silence in June with a rare disclosure of an earthbound L3Harris ASAT jammer—building toward potential deterrence disclosures at the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference. Lifting United States (0.49 -> 0.53) while trimming Russia (0.25 -> 0.23) and China (0.12 -> 0.10), with France (0.08, Yoda) and India (0.03) steady (sum = 0.97).
